mainTopic: The laws of washing for an אבל, and where the fast-day prayer is said and how many ברכות are added on public fasts.
overview: The amud opens with a debate about whether an אבל may bathe in cold water. In the first version, רבא allows it. A ברייתא about a בוגרת is used to challenge him, but the גמרא explains that the ברייתא is about eye-paint and hair-dye, not bathing. The story of רבי יוסי בר חנינא, who bathed in cold water all of שבעה, is rejected as a proof for רבא, because his mourning periods came one after another. In a second version, רבא forbids cold water, and the same ברייתא is tried as a support and rejected the same way. The final הלכה: an אבל may not wash his whole body in hot or cold water, may wash his face, hands and feet in cold water only, and may not anoint unless it is to remove dirt. The גמרא then returns to fast days and asks where an individual says the fast prayer. רב יצחק rules that it goes inside שומע תפלה, because an individual may not add his own ברכה. A long back-and-forth follows about how many ברכות the שליח צבור says on each series of public fasts, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A grown girl may not make herself unattractive while mourning her father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A בוגרת may not neglect her appearance during mourning for her father, but a נערה may.
steps.simpleTranslation: A grown girl is not allowed to make herself unattractive during the mourning days for her father. This implies that a young girl is allowed to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about how a grown girl behaves while she mourns. This is setup: in the next steps the גמרא will use it to test רבא's ruling about cold-water bathing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בוגרת is old enough to marry, so she must not make herself look bad, because that could hurt her chances of finding a match. A נערה is still young, so the ברייתא implies she may neglect her appearance like any other mourner.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl over twelve and a half, fully grown and ready for marriage
A girl between twelve and twelve and a half
To make unattractive, to neglect one's appearance

phrases.english: A grown girl is not permitted
to make herself unattractive
during the days of mourning for her father.
This implies: a young girl is permitted.
phrases.notes: The word הָא signals an inference drawn from the wording of the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין הַבּוֹגֶרֶת רַשָּׁאָה לְנַוֵּול אֶת עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test רבא's earlier ruling (on the previous amud) that an אבל may bathe in cold water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בוגרת may not neglect her appearance during mourning for her father. By implication, a נערה may.

steps.title: The leniency cannot be about hot water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is about bathing. It then shows it cannot mean hot water, because רב חסדא forbids a mourner even to put a finger into hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it talking about bathing? And in what kind of water? If you say hot water, is that really what a grown girl is allowed to do? But רב חסדא said that a mourner may not even stick his finger into hot water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא assumes the ברייתא's leniency is about bathing and asks which kind of water it means. It rules out hot water using רב חסדא's strict ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hot water is totally forbidden to any אבל, even just a finger. So the ברייתא cannot be letting a בוגרת bathe in hot water. This clears the way for the next step's conclusion that it must mean cold water.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility that will be rejected)
But didn't [so-and-so] say! (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: Is it not about bathing?
And in what [water]?
If you say in hot water,
is a grown girl [then] not permitted [to refrain]?!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: if the ברייתא meant hot water, it would be letting a בוגרת bathe in hot water during mourning. That is impossible, as רב חסדא's ruling shows next.

phrases.english: But didn't רב חסדא say:
A mourner is forbidden to put his finger into hot water!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו בִּרְחִיצָה, וּבְמַאי? אִילֵימָא בְּחַמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts working out what kind of leniency the ברייתא gives a בוגרת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the ברייתא permits hot-water bathing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא forbids even a finger in hot water for an אבל, so hot water cannot be the leniency.

steps.title: So it must be cold water, which challenges רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא lets a בוגרת bathe in cold water. That implies other mourners may not, which contradicts רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it about cold water?
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out hot water, the גמרא says the leniency must be cold water. This is the actual challenge against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only a בוגרת gets permission for cold water because of her special marriage concern, then a regular mourner, like a נערה, would be forbidden even cold water. That directly contradicts רבא's ruling that any אבל may bathe in cold water all seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it... (pushes toward the only remaining option)

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against the ברייתא. It is against רבא. The point is that a cold-water permission given specially to a בוגרת implies that ordinary mourners do not have it.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it [about] cold water?
phrases.notes: So a נערה, like an ordinary mourner, may not bathe even in cold water. This contradicts רבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the elimination from step 2 and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that an אבל may bathe in cold water all seven days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats cold-water bathing as a special leniency for a בוגרת, which implies it is forbidden to ordinary mourners.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about eye-paint and hair-dye, not bathing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not talking about bathing at all. It means cosmetics: eye-paint (כיחול) and hair-dye (פירכוס).
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about painting the eyes and dyeing the hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by changing what the ברייתא is about. The leniency for a בוגרת is cosmetics, not bathing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ברייתא is about makeup, it says nothing about bathing. רבא's ruling on cold water stands untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: Dyeing or arranging the hair (beautifying cosmetics)

phrases.english: No, [it refers] to eye-painting and hair-dyeing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the subject of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about bathing in cold water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about cosmetics, so it does not contradict רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the בוגרת is about make-up and hair-dye, so it poses no challenge to רבא's cold-water ruling.

steps.title: A proposed support: רבי יוסי בר חנינא bathed in cold water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a proof for רבא. When רבי יוסי בר חנינא's sons died, he bathed in cold water all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? רבי אבא הכהן said in the name of רבי יוסי הכהן: It once happened that the sons of רבי יוסי בר חנינא died, and he bathed in cold water all seven days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tries to support רבא with a real-life story. A great sage bathed in cold water throughout his שבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a great sage bathed in cold water during all seven days of mourning, that seems to prove an אבל may do so, just as רבא said. The word לימא hints that the גמרא may end up rejecting this proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
An incident, a story that happened

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him?
For רבי אבא הכהן said
in the name of רבי יוסי הכהן:
An incident: the sons died
of רבי יוסי בר חנינא,
and he bathed in cold water all seven [days]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defended רבא, the גמרא now looks for positive support for him.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that an אבל may bathe in cold water all seven days
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי יוסי בר חנינא, who bathed in cold water throughout שבעה

steps.title: His case was special: one mourning came right after another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יוסי בר חנינא had several mourning periods back-to-back, which allows special leniencies.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: there, it was a case where his mourning periods pressed on him one after another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the story. It says that case was an unusual situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since his sons died one after the other, he was in mourning for a long, continuous time. Washing was allowed for that special reason, so the story does not prove that an ordinary אבל may bathe in cold water.

keyTerms.meaning: They say (introduces an answer from the scholars)
His mourning periods pressed upon him (came back-to-back)

phrases.english: They say:
There, it was when his mourning periods pressed upon him
one after another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof only, not רבא's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story was an exceptional case of back-to-back mourning, so it cannot teach the general law.

steps.title: A ברייתא: back-to-back mourning allows trimming hair and washing clothes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up the rejection. When mourning periods come back-to-back, one may lighten heavy hair with a razor and wash clothing in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If his mourning periods came one after another and his hair became heavy, he may lighten it with a razor, and he may wash his garment in water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that back-to-back mourning really does allow extra leniencies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an אבל may not cut his hair or wash his clothes. When mourning periods pile up, the ברייתא allows relief. This supports the claim that רבי יוסי בר חנינא's cold-water bathing was a special leniency of that situation.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught:
If his mourning periods pressed upon him one after another,
[and] his hair grew heavy, he may lighten it with a razor,
and he may wash his garment in water.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: תְּכָפוּהוּ אֲבָלָיו זֶה אַחַר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the exception named in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that back-to-back mourning allows special leniencies
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא permitting hair-trimming and clothes-washing in that case

steps.title: רב חסדא limits the leniencies: razor only, plain water only
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the leniencies are limited. Hair may be cut with a razor but not scissors, and clothes washed with water but not with cleaning agents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: With a razor, but not with scissors. With water, but not with natron, sand, or אהל (a soap-plant).
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא clarifies the exact limits of the ברייתא's leniencies, so the mourner still keeps some sign of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A razor gives a rougher trim than scissors, so the mourner does not look fully groomed. Plain water washes clothes without the full cleaning that natron, sand, or soap-plant would give. Even in this exceptional case, the relief is partial.
steps.whatToRemember: The cold-water story of רבי יוסי בר חנינא does not prove רבא, because back-to-back mourning has its own leniencies. Even those leniencies are limited: razor and not scissors, plain water and not cleaning agents.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
With a razor, but not with scissors;
in water, but not with natron,
and not with sand, and not with ahal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּתַעַר אֲבָל לֹא בְּמִסְפָּרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the precise meaning of the ברייתא's words in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In back-to-back mourning, hair may be lightened only with a razor, and clothes washed only with plain water.

steps.title: Second version: רבא forbids cold-water bathing
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the discussion, רבא rules that an אבל may not bathe even in cold water during all of שבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version: רבא said: A mourner is forbidden to bathe in cold water all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second version (איכא דאמרי) of רבא's ruling. In this version רבא is strict: an אבל may not bathe even in cold water for all seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was working with a version where רבא allowed cold water. This new version flips his position to a prohibition. The rest of this section will test this stricter view.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say — introduces a second version of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first version רבא allowed cold water. In this second version רבא forbids it. Each version gets its own back-and-forth.

phrases.english: Some say (a different version):
Rava said:
A mourner is forbidden to bathe in cold water all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second version of רבא's ruling that is the opposite of the first version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not bathe in cold water during all seven days of mourning.

steps.title: Why is this different from meat and wine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: if an אבל may enjoy meat and wine, why can't he bathe in cold water?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different here from meat and wine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's strict ruling. An אבל is allowed to eat meat and drink wine, so why should cold water be forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat and wine are real pleasures, yet an אבל may have them. If pleasure is allowed there, it seems odd to forbid the smaller comfort of cold water. The question asks רבא to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (a challenge asking to explain a distinction)

phrases.english: What is different from meat and wine (which a mourner may have)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that cold water is forbidden to an אבל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אבל may enjoy meat and wine, so forbidding a smaller comfort like cold water seems inconsistent.

steps.title: Meat and wine calm the mourner's distress
steps.stepSummary: Meat and wine are allowed because they help the אבל calm his anxiety, not because pleasure is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he does it to relieve his anxiety.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that meat and wine are a special case. They are allowed because they help the mourner calm down from his grief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat and wine are permitted for a purpose: they soothe the mourner's distress. Bathing in cold water does not serve that purpose, so the general ban on bathing still applies. This explains the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: There — referring to the other case

phrases.english: There (with meat and wine), to relieve his anxiety
is why he does it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since meat and wine are allowed, all comforts should be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Meat and wine are allowed only because they ease the mourner's distress; bathing has no such purpose.

steps.title: A proposed proof from the grown woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא about a בוגרת supports רבא. It infers that a נערה may make herself unattractive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him: A grown woman is not permitted to make herself unattractive. This implies a young woman is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a support for רבא's strict view from a ברייתא about a grown woman in mourning. It reads the ברייתא to mean that a young girl may make herself unattractive. This sets up the next step, which asks what kind of washing is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a בוגרת may not make herself look neglected. The inference is that a נערה may, meaning she skips some kind of washing. The גמרא still needs to figure out which washing this is.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
To make herself unattractive or neglected

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
A grown woman is not permitted to make herself unattractive.
This implies that a young girl is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבא, the גמרא now looks for a source that supports him.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that cold water is forbidden to an אבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a בוגרת not making herself unattractive

steps.title: It can't mean hot water, so it must mean cold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the ברייתא can't be about hot water, since hot water is forbidden to every אבל. So it must be about cold water, which supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what? If you say hot water — is a grown woman not permitted to refrain? But רב חסדא said: A mourner may not even put his finger in hot water! Rather, isn't it about cold water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes building the proof. Hot water can't be meant, because every mourner is already forbidden in hot water. So the ברייתא must be talking about cold water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If hot water were meant, the ברייתא would make no sense: no mourner may use hot water, per רב חסדא. So the washing the נערה may skip must be cold water. That means cold water is normally forbidden to an אבל, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? (leads to the intended conclusion)

phrases.english: With what (kind of water)? If you say hot water:
Is a grown woman not permitted (to refrain from washing)?!
But didn't Rav Chisda say:
A mourner is forbidden to put his finger into hot water!
Rather, isn't it talking about cold water?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 12 by ruling out hot water.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that cold water is forbidden to an אבל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a בוגרת, read together with רב חסדא's ban on hot water

steps.title: No — the source is about cosmetics
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ברייתא is about eye-paint and hair-dye, not bathing.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is about eye-paint and hair-dye.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא is not about bathing at all. It is about eye-paint and hair-dye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is about cosmetics, it says nothing about cold water. So the proof for רבא falls away. This is the same answer the גמרא gave in the first version, now used again in the second version.

phrases.english: No, it is about eye-paint and hair-dye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 12-13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רבא's ruling itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא was about washing, but it can be read as being about cosmetics.

steps.title: רב חסדא: laundering is forbidden all seven days
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא infers that an אבל normally may not launder clothes during all of שבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This means that a mourner is forbidden to launder all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא learns a new rule from the earlier sources. An אבל may not do laundry for all seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing clothes was allowed only as a special leniency when mourning periods came back-to-back. That shows that in a normal case, laundering is forbidden for the whole שבעה. רב חסדא spells out this inference.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a special leniency teaches us the normal rule: if something is allowed only in an unusual case, it is normally forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: This means:
A mourner is forbidden to launder all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical inference from the leniency for back-to-back mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normally, an אבל may not launder clothes during all seven days.

steps.title: The final הלכה on washing and anointing
steps.stepSummary: Final ruling: the whole body may not be washed in hot or cold water. Face, hands and feet may be washed in cold water only. Anointing is forbidden unless it is to remove dirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: A mourner may not wash his whole body, in hot or cold water, all seven days. But his face, hands and feet — in hot water it is forbidden, in cold water it is permitted. Anointing, even a tiny amount, is forbidden. But if it is to remove dirt, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical הלכה for an אבל about washing and anointing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing the whole body is fully forbidden, whether hot or cold, so the final הלכה agrees with the strict view. Face, hands and feet are lighter: cold water is fine, hot water is not. Anointing for pleasure is forbidden, but anointing just to remove dirt is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: To anoint (smear oil on the skin)

steps.whatToRemember: An אבל: no washing of the whole body (hot or cold); face, hands and feet are allowed in cold water only; no anointing, unless it is to remove dirt.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
A mourner is forbidden to wash his whole body

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּחַמִּין וּבֵין בְּצוֹנֵן כׇּל שִׁבְעָה.
phrases.english: whether in hot water or in cold water, all seven days.
But his face, his hands, and his feet:
in hot water it is forbidden; in cold water it is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לָסוּךְ, אֲפִילּוּ כָּל שֶׁהוּא אָסוּר.
phrases.english: But anointing, even the smallest amount, is forbidden.
But if it is to remove the dirt, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole mourning discussion with the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whole-body washing is forbidden in hot or cold water. Face, hands and feet may be washed in cold water only. Anointing is forbidden except to remove dirt.

steps.title: How do we mention the fast in prayer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the topic of תענית and asks how the special fast-day prayer is said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prayer of a fast — how do we mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the mourning topic and goes back to fast days. It asks how and where the special fast-day prayer (עננו) is said. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, a return to the laws of תענית. The question is practical: in which part of the תפילה do we add the fast-day prayer?

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer of a fast day (עננו)

phrases.english: The prayer of a fast — how do we mention it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, returning to the laws of fast days.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How and where the fast-day prayer is inserted in the עמידה

steps.title: Insert it between גואל and רופא
steps.stepSummary: A teaching delivered through רב יהודה and his son רב יצחק rules that an individual who takes on a fast says the fast prayer between the ברכות of גואל and רופא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה guided his son רב יצחק, and he taught: An individual who accepted a fast upon himself prays the fast prayer. And where does he say it? Between גואל ('Who redeems') and רופא ('Who heals').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. An individual who took on a fast says the fast prayer, and he places it between the ברכה of גואל ישראל and the ברכה of רופא חולי עמו ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rashi reads אַדְבְּרֵיהּ to mean that רב יהודה used his son רב יצחק as his spokesman (מתורגמן), and that רב יהודה himself expounded. This explains why רב יצחק objects to the teaching in the next step. The rule: an individual faster says the fast prayer, between the seventh and eighth ברכות of the עמידה.

keyTerms.meaning: He guided him (and gave him permission to teach publicly)
Who accepted a fast upon himself

steps.whatToRemember: An individual who takes on a fast says the fast prayer between the ברכות of גואל and רופא.

phrases.aramaic: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda guided his son Rav Yitzchak (to teach publicly),
and he taught:
An individual who accepted a fast upon himself
prays the prayer of a fast.
And where does he say it?
Between 'Who redeems' and 'Who heals'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְבְּרֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ, וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An individual faster says the fast prayer, inserted between the ברכות of גואל and רופא.

steps.title: Can an individual create his own blessing?
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק objects to placing the fast prayer as a separate ברכה between גואל and רופא, since an individual may not set up his own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק challenged this: Can an individual really set up a new blessing for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק attacks the ruling from the previous step that an individual says the fast prayer between גואל and רופא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the fast prayer between גואל and רופא makes it a separate, extra ברכה in the עמידה. רב יצחק argues that only a community, through the שליח צבור, may add a whole ברכה. A private person may not change the fixed structure of the עמידה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets up a separate, independent blessing
The 7th and 8th ברכות of the עמידה (redemption and healing)

phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak strongly objected to it:
But may an individual establish a blessing for himself?
phrases.notes: A separate ברכה between גואל and רופא would be an extra, independent blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the placement of the fast prayer given in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an individual says the fast prayer between גואל and רופא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Placing it there makes it a separate ברכה, and an individual may not add a ברכה of his own to the עמידה.

steps.title: The fast prayer goes inside שומע תפלה
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק rules that an individual adds the fast prayer within the ברכה of שומע תפלה, and רב ששת says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יצחק said: He says it in שומע תפלה ('Who listens to prayer'). And רב ששת said the same: in שומע תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the earlier placement, רב יצחק gives his own answer: the fast prayer is added inside שומע תפלה. רב ששת agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שומע תפלה is a general request that our prayers be accepted, so any private request may be added there. This way the individual mentions his fast without creating a new ברכה. The count of ברכות stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who listens to prayer': the general ברכה where private requests may be added
And likewise said (a second Amora agreeing)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה followed today: an individual says עננו inside שומע תפלה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yitzchak said:
In 'Who listens to prayer.'
And similarly, Rav Sheshet said:
In 'Who listens to prayer.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected placement with a new ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual who is fasting includes the fast prayer within שומע תפלה, not as a separate ברכה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: individual says 18, community says 19
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying the only difference between an individual and a community on a fast is 18 versus 19 ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: The only difference between an individual and a community is that this one prays eighteen and that one prays nineteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב יצחק. This step only quotes the source. The next steps work out what it means and how it challenges him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says one side adds a nineteenth ברכה on a fast. If that side could be a private person, it would show that an individual may add a ברכה, against רב יצחק. The challenge depends on who 'community' refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)
Nineteen: the regular עמידה plus one extra fast ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: Today's עמידה actually has 19 ברכות, but the ברייתא uses the classic name 'שמונה עשרה' for the ordinary עמידה. Here '18' means 'the normal עמידה' and '19' means 'the normal עמידה plus one extra fast ברכה.'

phrases.english: They raised an objection: There is no difference between an individual and a community,
except that this one prays eighteen,
and that one prays nineteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a source that may contradict רב יצחק's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יצחק's view that an individual may not add a ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא may describe a person who adds a nineteenth ברכה; the next steps check whether that person is an individual.

steps.title: Who are the 'individual' and the 'community'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means and shows that 'community' cannot simply mean the שליח צבור, because the שליח צבור says 24 ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'individual' and what is 'community'? If you say 'individual' means a real individual and 'community' means the prayer leader, does he say nineteen? He says twenty-four!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא analyzes the ברייתא to find out who each side is. It tests the simple reading and finds a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading is that 'community' means the שליח צבור leading a public fast. But on a public fast the שליח צבור adds six ברכות, making 24, not 19. So the simple reading seems not to fit the ברייתא's numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (proposing a reading to test it)
The prayer leader who prays on behalf of the community
Twenty-four: 18 plus six extra fast ברכות

phrases.english: What is 'individual' and what is 'community'?
If we say 'individual' means an actual individual,
and 'community' means the prayer leader,
are those nineteen?
They are twenty-four!
phrases.notes: On public fasts the שליח צבור adds six special ברכות (taught in the next פרק).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who does the ברייתא mean by 'individual' and 'community'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For now, the simple reading (community = שליח צבור) seems ruled out because he says 24, not 19. Step 23 offers the alternative reading (two individuals), and step 24 restores the simple reading by limiting the ברייתא to the first three fasts.

steps.title: So an individual on a communal fast adds a ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as two individuals, one on a private fast (18) and one on a communal fast (19), which would prove an individual can add a ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what it means: The only difference between an individual who took on a private fast and an individual who took on a communal fast is that this one prays eighteen and that one prays nineteen. Learn from this: an individual may set up a blessing for himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers the only reading that seems to fit, and it turns the ברייתא into a proof against רב יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both sides are private people, then a private person on a communal fast says a separate ברכה, making 19. That directly shows an individual can set up a ברכה, which is exactly what רב יצחק denied.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that (introducing the forced reading)
This is what it is saying
Learn from this (conclusion of a proof)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין יָחִיד דְּקִבֵּל עָלָיו תַּעֲנִית יָחִיד
phrases.english: There is no difference between an individual who accepted upon himself a private fast
and an individual who accepted upon himself a communal fast,
except that this one prays eighteen,
and that one prays nineteen.
Learn from this:
An individual may establish a blessing for himself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having ruled out the simple reading in Step 22, offers the reading that proves against רב יצחק.
steps.raayaObject: That an individual may set up a separate ברכה for himself, against רב יצחק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, read as an individual on a communal fast praying 19.

steps.title: The 19 refers to the שליח צבור on the first three fasts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: 'community' does mean the שליח צבור, and the ברייתא speaks of the first three communal fasts, when he adds only one ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, I can tell you it means the prayer leader. And as for your difficulty that the prayer leader prays twenty-four: this refers to the first three fasts, when there are not twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof and returns to the simple reading. It answers the earlier problem of the 24 ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 24 ברכות are only said on the later, more severe public fasts. On the first three communal fasts, the שליח צבור adds just one ברכה (עננו), making 19. So the ברייתא contrasts a private person (18) with the שליח צבור (19), and רב יצחק's rule that an individual may not add a ברכה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (keeping the original reading)
And as for what troubles you
The first three public fasts for rain, the lighter ones

steps.whatToRemember: An individual who fasts adds עננו inside שומע תפלה and never adds a separate ברכה. Only the שליח צבור adds a separate ברכה: one extra on the first three public fasts (19), and six extra on the later severe fasts (24).

phrases.aramaic: לָא, לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר,
phrases.english: No, actually I will tell you it means the prayer leader,
and as for what is difficult for you:
the prayer leader prays twenty-four,
the ברייתא is about the first three fasts,
when there are not twenty-four.
phrases.notes: On those fasts the שליח צבור says 18 plus one, which is 19.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 23 by answering the problem raised in Step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא as two individuals, and with it the proof against רב יצחק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the שליח צבור always says 24. But on the first three fasts he says only 19, so the ברייתא can refer to him.

steps.title: A ברייתא implies the first and middle fasts are equal regarding 24 ברכות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the only difference between the first three and middle three fasts is about work. This implies both series are the same regarding the 24 ברכות, which goes against the claim that the first three have only one added ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is that not so? But the ברייתא teaches 'the only difference': The only difference between the first three fasts and the middle three fasts is that on these, work is permitted, and on these, work is forbidden. This implies that regarding twenty-four ברכות, both are the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 24, which said the שליח צבור adds only one ברכה on the first three fasts. It brings a ברייתא that seems to say the first three and the middle three fasts are equal regarding the 24 ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only one difference between the first and middle series: whether מלאכה is allowed. The words 'אֵין בֵּין' mean 'there is no difference except this one.' So in everything else, including 24 ברכות, the two series should be the same. If the middle fasts have 24, then the first fasts have 24 too, and step 24's answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is no difference between… except' – a formula listing the only difference

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge assumes the middle three fasts DO have the full 24 ברכות. That assumption is what lets the ברייתא 'drag' the first three fasts up to 24 as well.

phrases.english: And is that not so?
phrases.notes: Questions step 24's claim that on the first three fasts only one ברכה is added.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'the only difference between':

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין שָׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת לְשָׁלֹשׁ אֶמְצָעִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: There is no difference between the first three and the middle three fasts,
except that on these (the first) one is permitted to do work,
and on these (the middle) one is forbidden to do work.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע — זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין!
phrases.english: This implies that regarding twenty-four blessings, both are the same!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the דחיה of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 24's claim that the שליח צבור adds only one ברכה on the first three fasts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אֵין בֵּין' means work is the only difference, so the first and middle fasts are equal regarding 24 ברכות.

steps.title: The תנא listed some differences and left others out
steps.stepSummary: The proposed answer is that the ברייתא is not a complete list. The תנא simply left out the difference about ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught some and left some out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a quick answer: the ברייתא does not mention every difference. The difference about the 24 ברכות was just left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the list is incomplete, nothing can be learned from what it does not say. Then the first three fasts can still have only 19 ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא taught some cases and left some out

phrases.english: He taught and left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The list in the ברייתא is not complete
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'אֵין בֵּין' list is complete, so the two series are equal in everything else.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list is partial, so the ברכות difference could simply be missing.

steps.title: Two problems with the 'left out' answer
steps.stepSummary: The 'left out' answer is attacked in two ways. First, nothing else was left out, and a תנא would not leave out just one item. Second, 'אֵין בֵּין' means 'only this difference.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What else did he leave out, that we should say he left out this too? And furthermore: it teaches 'the only difference'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'left out' answer with two arguments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that you can only say 'he left something out' if there is at least one other omitted item. Here no other omission can be found. On top of that, the wording 'אֵין בֵּין' clearly claims to be the full list.

keyTerms.meaning: What else did he omit, that this was also omitted?

phrases.english: What else did he leave out, that he left out this?
phrases.notes: A single omission is not accepted. There needs to be another omitted item.

phrases.english: And furthermore: it teaches 'the only difference'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the תירוץ of step 26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no second omission, and the wording 'אֵין בֵּין' signals a complete list.

steps.title: The ברייתא only discusses prohibitions, not prayers
steps.stepSummary: The new answer is that the ברייתא is only comparing the restrictions of the fasts. It says nothing at all about the prayers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תנא is speaking about prohibitions. He is not speaking about prayers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a better answer: the ברייתא's 'only difference' applies only to the topic of what is forbidden on the fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אֵין בֵּין' can be fully true within its own topic. Among the prohibitions, work really is the only difference. Prayers are a separate topic the ברייתא never covered, so it proves nothing about the 24 ברכות.

phrases.english: Rather, the תנא is speaking about prohibitions,
he is not speaking about prayers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 26 with a new answer to step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the topic of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אֵין בֵּין' covers every topic, including prayers.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אֵין בֵּין' covers only prohibitions, so prayers may still differ.

steps.title: Even the middle fasts do not have 24 ברכות
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the first and middle fasts really are equal. Neither one has 24 ברכות. Only the last seven fasts do.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: on the middle fasts too, he does not pray twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer. It agrees the two series are the same, but says the 24 ברכות belong only to the last seven fasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא assumed the middle fasts have 24 ברכות. This answer denies that assumption. So 'זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין' is true: both series have no 24 ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (an alternative answer)

phrases.english: And if you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶמְצָעֲיָיתָא נָמֵי לָא מְצַלֵּי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע.
phrases.english: on the middle fasts too, he does not pray twenty-four.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּאֶמְצָעֲיָיתָא נָמֵי לָא מְצַלֵּי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the hidden assumption of the קשיא
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the last seven fasts have 24 ברכות. The first and middle series are equal in not having them.

steps.title: Another ברייתא implies the middle fasts do have 24 ברכות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the middle three and last seven fasts differ only in sounding alarms and closing shops. This implies they are equal in everything else, including 24 ברכות. And 'he left it out' cannot be said, because the ברייתא uses 'אֵין בֵּין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is that not so? But it was taught: The only difference between the second three fasts and the last seven is that on these they sound alarms and lock the shops. This implies that in all their other matters, both are the same! And if you say that here too he taught and left out — but it teaches 'the only difference'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second answer from step 29. It brings another ברייתא suggesting that the middle fasts are just like the last seven, which do have 24 ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last seven fasts have 24 ברכות. If the middle fasts differ from them only in התרעה and closing shops, then the middle fasts have 24 as well. The 'תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר' escape is blocked by the wording 'אֵין בֵּין', just as in step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: The second three fasts (the middle series)
They sound an alarm (shofar or trumpets)

phrases.english: And is that not so?! But it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין שָׁלֹשׁ שְׁנִיּוֹת לְשֶׁבַע אַחֲרוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: There is no difference between the second three and the last seven,
except that on these they sound alarms
and lock the shops.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶן — זֶה וָזֶה שָׁוִין!
phrases.english: This implies that in all their other matters, both are the same!

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר —
phrases.english: And if you say that here too he taught and left out —
but it teaches 'the only difference'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא?! וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵין בֵּין שָׁלֹשׁ שְׁנִיּוֹת לְשֶׁבַע אַחֲרוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second answer from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the middle fasts do not have 24 ברכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The middle fasts equal the last seven in everything except alarms and shops, so they too have 24 ברכות. 'תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר' is blocked by 'אֵין בֵּין'.

steps.title: Is 'אֵין בֵּין' really meant to be exact?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with a counter-question. Do you really think 'אֵין בֵּין' means there is truly only one difference? This opens the way to showing that it is not exact.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really think that 'the only difference' is exact?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the attack with a rhetorical question. This sets up its next move, where it will show that 'אֵין בֵּין' is not meant to be taken word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיאות of steps 27 and 30 both relied on reading 'אֵין בֵּין' as a complete list. The גמרא now questions that very assumption. If other differences between the series can be found, then 'אֵין בֵּין' is not precise, and the ברייתא does not prove the middle fasts have 24 ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (a rhetorical counter-question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a question in form, but it works as the start of an answer. The גמרא is about to show that 'אֵין בֵּין' leaves out other differences too.

phrases.english: And can you really think that 'the only difference' is exact?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the response to step 30 by questioning its premise.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Challenging the premise that 'אֵין בֵּין' is a complete list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אֵין בֵּין' means there is truly only one difference.
steps.terutzMaskana: (To be shown next) 'אֵין בֵּין' is not exact, so 'תְּנָא וְשַׁיַּיר' is possible.
